name: Intralesional cortisone injection

lead: An intralesional cortisone injection is a clinic procedure in which a corticosteroid is injected directly into an inflamed acne cyst or nodule. People with a large painful spot before an event use it for a flatter, less red pimple, often described as shrinking overnight.

The corticosteroid delivers anti-inflammatory action right at the inflamed tissue, so swelling drops. Wikipedia lists it among acne procedures and describes it as offering rapid relief. Trial detail was not covered in the sources reviewed.

paras: It is a quick in-office procedure done by a dermatologist or clinician for individual large lesions, and people often book it ahead of an occasion.

The sources give little detail on side effects. Glucocorticoids are noted to be able to worsen acne in general, and corticosteroids can affect the skin locally. The procedure is performed by clinicians.

chain: Swelling drops within a day or two
angle.text: A clinician injects steroid into a big inflamed cyst, and swelling and redness drop within a day or two for a visibly flatter pimple. The flattening is widely reported in appearance communities.

lead: An intralesional cortisone injection is a procedure in which a clinician injects a corticosteroid directly into an inflamed lesion, such as a painful acne cyst or nodule. In appearance-focused communities it is discussed as a way to flatten a large pimple quickly, often described as shrinking a cyst "overnight".

Wikipedia lists injection of a corticosteroid into an inflamed acne lesion among the procedures used for acne, describing it as offering rapid relief [1]. Triamcinolone acetonide, a synthetic glucocorticoid, is one corticosteroid injected into skin lesions such as keloids and hypertrophic scars [2].
infobox: Inflamed acne lesions [1]; keloids and hypertrophic scars [2]

paras: The procedure delivers a corticosteroid into the lesion itself rather than onto the skin surface or through the bloodstream. For acne, Wikipedia places it under procedural treatments, alongside comedo extraction, and states it is intended for inflamed lesions [1].
Triamcinolone acetonide is described as a glucocorticoid roughly five times as potent as cortisol with very little mineralocorticoid activity, and its injection into scars is a recognised use [2].

The sources reviewed for this article do not itemise the adverse effects of intralesional injection into acne lesions. Wikipedia notes more generally that glucocorticoid medications can worsen existing acne [1], and that corticosteroids can have endocrine effects [2]. Because the procedure is performed by clinicians, the specifics of agent selection and technique are a matter for medical practice.
No studies found. Wikipedia describes the injection as a procedure for acne relief but the pages reviewed do not summarise trial results [1].
